usage.title: A few notes
usage.point1Text: You don't need to ask permission to use the badge, logo, or link to this site. Grab them, hotlink them, slap them on your website. I don't care. Actually, I'd be delighted.
usage.point2Text: If you're using the badge, please use image-rendering: pixelated (or crisp-edges for Firefox) in your CSS. Without it, browsers will blur the pixels and it'll look like garbage. It's pixel art, please treat it like pixel art.
usage.point3Text: If you're writing about the site or using these in a blog post or article, a link back would be appreciated. But if you're just adding my badge to your links page, you don't need to do anything extra. My HTML snippet for the badge itself already links here.
usage.point4Text: Don't use these to impersonate me, claim I endorsed something I didn't, or make it look like I'm affiliated with something sketchy. I trust you know the difference between linking to a site you like and pretending to be someone else. If you're unsure whether what you're doing is weird, it probably is.
usage.footer: That's it, just use them respectfully and we're good.

colophon.title: Colophon
colophon.description: How I built this site and what I write in.
colophon.intro: I registered the domain in late 2023 and somehow turned a basic personal homepage into a place for economics posts and cats. I tinker with it whenever I find something that could be a little nicer, which happens a lot.

technology.title: How it's built
technology.build: Astro builds the pages into static HTML. Tailwind does most of the styling, and bits of TypeScript and Preact handle the games. You can read the blog with JavaScript off, but not so much with Tetris.
technology.history: The first version was WordPress on some sketchy free hosting. Then came Carrd, Astro, then a stint with Next.js, during which I gave a personal website more architecture than it knew what to do with. I moved back to Astro for version 5 in April 2026. Turns out I mostly wanted to write some words and put them on the internet after all.
technology.hosting: Netlify serves the main site, Vercel serves the backup at z.is-a.dev, there's a simple copy on Neocities too. Cloudflare handles DNS and proxies the main domain. Being able to take the same site somewhere else is a big part of why I like building it this way.
technology.migration: How I moved back to Astro

writing.title: Writing and editing
writing.body: Posts are Markdown files in the repo, with a bit of frontmatter for the metadata. There's a field for whether a cat approved the post (spoiler, it always does). Images can be right there with the text. The /now page and the devlog use JSON, the interface translations are in their files. Publishing a post is basically just committing a file and waiting for the build to deploy.
writing.images: There’s a little shortcut for screenshots. When I put a Markdown image in a paragraph of its own with alt text, a small script also shows that text as a caption. One less bit of markup to type every time I want to show a screenshot.

typography.title: Typography
typography.body: Lexend is my default for headings and body text. The fonts live on the site, Chinese and Hán Nôm have their dedicated fonts. If you'd rather read in Atkinson Hyperlegible, OpenDyslexic or just use your system font, they're in the settings. That menu lets you turn off the stars or turn up the contrast too by the way.

components.title: The bits I keep tinkering with
components.body: The homepage gets a random mood cat and you can press R on your keyboard for another one. I also made a keyboard command palette, a retro version for older browsers and a tools page for things I got tired of doing by hand. Somewhere in there I added 2048 and Tetris. It was supposed to be a personal website, well, technically it still is.

follow.title: Keeping up
follow.body: The blog has RSS, Atom, and JSON feeds. If a page is awkward to use with a keyboard or something looks broken on your setup, I'd like to hear about it.

privacy.title: What happens when you visit
privacy.body: I use Umami to count visits on the main site and the Vercel backup. Your browser stores preferences like the theme and font locally. If you sign the guestbook, the form goes through Netlify Forms.

licenses.title: Reuse and credits
licenses.body: The code is under the AGPL, version 3 or later. My writing and other original non-code content are under CC BY 4.0. If you reuse my work, please credit me and link back. Other people’s fonts, cursors, badges, and images keep their own terms.

inspiration.body: I liked the way Maggie Appleton explains her own site. Her colophon sent me to Gwern's, too.
